transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mrs. Al-Rashid. It is good to see you again, although I wish it were under better circumstances. How are you feeling right now?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am very confused, doctor. My wound is open. I felt the pain coming back and then the bleeding started. I do not understand why this is happening.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it is very upsetting to be back in the hospital so soon. I have looked at your charts and the wound.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I did everything you told me. I rested. I was very careful. Why did the stitches not hold?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the timing of your discharge yesterday. Things didn't go quite right with the schedule.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? What do you mean? You told me it was time to go home. I trusted you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the coordination of the discharge papers. It happened faster than it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand. Did someone make a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system for tracking the post-operative hours was not followed perfectly. It is a very busy unit, and the paperwork was processed early.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I am here now. My leg is bleeding. I was so happy to be going home. Now I am scared.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. We are going to fix this now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is this common? For the doctors to be confused about when a patient can leave?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: These things can happen in a large hospital. It is just how the workflow is sometimes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know why I am in pain again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We need to focus on the clinical side of the wound now. I'm going to have the nurse clean the area.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I was sent away too soon. Was I?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some discrepancies in the timing of the protocols.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Please, doctor, just tell me. Did I come home too early?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a bit premature based on the standard window.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am very disappointed. I thought the care here was the best. I feel very lost.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughter said I should have stayed. I told her you are the expert. I believed you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a difficult situation for everyone.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What will happen to me now? Will I have to have the surgery again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see how the cleaning goes. I think we can manage it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When can I actually go home this time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how you progress over the next few hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot go back and forth like this. My family is worried.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that it is an inconvenience.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Was it my fault? Did I do something wrong at home?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, you followed the instructions. It was just a matter of the timing of the exit.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you are saying the hospital made a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a breakdown in the communication process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very distressing. I have never had this happen before.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. But we are here now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What is the plan to make sure this doesn't happen again tonight?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep a close eye on you. Just stay tuned for an update from the nursing staff.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan, doctor. What exactly are you doing for my leg?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to monitor the drainage. We'll likely just wait and see.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the discharge? When is that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I cannot give you a time yet. We will just have to see.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very shaken. I don't know who to trust.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's going to be okay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you won't tell me what happened. You keep talking about systems and confusion.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a timing issue with the protocol.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is that the only thing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that is the main point.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wanted to be healed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will the chief doctor be informed of this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make a note of it in the file.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very small in this big building.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So, what happens next?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The nurse will be in shortly. We'll just see how it goes.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and maintains a regulated tone despite the patient's repeated pushback.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes and hedging such as 'things didn't go quite right' and 'confusion' without explicitly naming the error until the patient repeatedly prompts them, and never checks for comprehension.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is consistently deflected to 'the system', 'the workflow', and 'communication process'.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation like 'I understand' and 'I know this is frustrating' but does not name specific emotions back to the patient.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders such as 'we'll see how it goes' and 'stay tuned', with no specific timelines or patient role.
